about: A bare `--` stops flag interpretation: everything after it is a value, however much it looks like a flag. Arguments can also require, or preserve, the separator.

vectors.doc: After `--`, a flag-looking word binds as a value.
Flags before the separator parse normally.

After the separator a word no longer routes, so `ex -- install` passes the string `install` to the argument instead of running the command. Stopping flag interpretation stops command selection with it: both are ways a token can mean something other than data.
The separator itself is consumed rather than bound to an argument.
Only the first `--` separates; a later one is an ordinary value, since flag interpretation has already stopped.
A variadic after the separator collects the whole tail verbatim, which is how a wrapper CLI forwards an inner command line untouched.
An argument declared `double_dash="required"` accepts a value once the separator has been given.
The same argument rejects a value given before the separator.
The default, `double_dash="optional"`, accepts a value on either side of the separator.
With `double_dash="preserve"`, the separator is kept as a value instead of being consumed — needed by CLIs that pass along command lines containing their own separators.
With `double_dash="automatic"`, the first value an argument takes stops flag interpretation for everything after it, so a wrapper can forward flags without the caller typing `--`.
A separator at the very end is a value too, since flag parsing stopped at the first one. This is the command line from the report that first raised it: `-- hello -- goodbye --`.
A variadic takes every remaining word, so nothing can follow it — except an argument that requires a `--`, which is exactly what stops the variadic. mise declares this on `run`, `exec` and `git`.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
arg "[args]" var=#true
arg "[-- rest]" var=#true

vectors.doc: Without the `--`, the first variadic keeps everything and the second stays empty — which is why mise declares it optional.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
arg "[args]" var=#true
arg "[-- rest]" var=#true

vectors.doc: Each variadic counts its own words. A bounded one before the `--` must not lend its count to the argument after it, which would otherwise stop early or at once.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
arg "[first]" var=#true var_max=3
arg "[-- rest]" var=#true var_max=2
